Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: days before a client counts as lapsed, days without a touch, the passport validity you want after a trip, the days to flag a special date and the largest gift.
Check Advisors, Clients and Trips. They hold the people, clients and trips that every other sheet looks up. Each client has an advisor, a source and a loyalty tier.
Set Loyalty Tiers: the trips or the sales that earn each tier. The Clients sheet shows the earned tier and tells you when a client should move up.
Write each client profile on Client Profiles, each preference on Travel Preferences and each person who travels with them on Companions.
Record special dates on Special Dates and the offers you send on Birthday and Anniversary Offers. Anniversary Trips Due lists the next trips to suggest.
Log every contact on Touchpoints and every note on Client Notes with a follow-up date. Overdue follow-ups and clients without a touch are flagged for you.

Keep Passport and Visa Watch up to date for every traveller on a coming trip. The risk check compares the expiry with the trip end date and your validity setting. Always check the destination current rules.
Track Referrals, Reviews and Past Trip Ideas. Referrals show the sales and commission each referral brought, Reviews flags a low rating that needs a reply.
Work the Win-back List every month: the reason, the offer and the status of each client who has not travelled for a long time.
Use Client Segments, Newsletter List and Clients by Month to see which groups of clients are worth a campaign and how repeat business changes month by month.
Use the 14 calculators for lifetime value, repeat scores, next trip ideas, the contact plan, referrals, win-back offers, passports, concentration, segments, review timing, gifts and what-ifs.
Read the Client Dashboard and Charts every week: repeat share, reviews, referrals, contacts due, passports at risk and win-back status.
Send every traveller off ready, with nothing missing
the destination's lead days turn a travel date into due dates for documents, visa, itinerary, vouchers and briefing

every voucher shows when it arrived, when you sent it and whether it went out in time
cover dates and amount against the trip dates and cost show gaps at the start or the end
every room, meal, access and celebration request shows the supplier asked, the answer and when to chase
Support log for trips in progress
each case on the road shows hours to solve against your target and which cases are still open
the new plan, the supplier refund and the client share give the cost left to the agency
Departure radar for the next 60 days
departures by week, documents missing and the ready check put the trips at risk first

One row per trip: client, destination, dates, status and advisor; days to departure, open documents, the ready check, vouchers to send and itinerary days fill in by themselves.
One row per planned day: trip, day number, date, place, activity and the booking behind it; the weekday, the client and the supplier fill in by themselves.
Bookings with confirmations and travel dates
One row per supplier booking: trip, supplier, confirmation, travel dates and status; days to travel, vouchers sent and the supplier phone fill in by themselves.
Travel documents by traveller and deadline
One row per document a client must send or you must send: kind, status, due date and received date; days to the deadline, days early, the risk check and the departure date fill in by themselves.
Your own planning notes for 24 destinations: passport months, visa days, health, insurance and entry-form reminders. Always check current rules; lead days fill in.
Passport validity and visa status by traveller
One row per traveller check: passport expiry, visa status and check date; months valid after the return, the last safe expiry date, the visa apply-by date and the checks fill in by themselves.
Travel insurance policies with cover gaps
One row per policy: insurer, policy number, cover dates and premium; days covered, the trip dates and a gap check fill in by themselves.
Vouchers and e-tickets sent to clients
One row per voucher or ticket: booking, kind, date it arrived from the supplier and date you sent it; days sent before travel and a send check fill in by themselves.
One row per task before a trip leaves: task, due date, who owns it and when it was done; days late and a task check fill in by themselves.
One row per briefing: trip, date, kind and the date the notes went out; days before departure, the notes check, the client and the phone fill in by themselves.
Packing and weather notes by destination and season
Typical planning figures for 40 destination and season pairs, with the note you send; check a current forecast first. Clothing advice, rain advice and trips to the place fill in by themselves.
One row per trip: local contact, hotel, supplier desk and phone numbers, and the time zone of the place; the hours of difference, the client and the advisor phone fill in by themselves.
In-trip support cases and time to solve
One row per case on a trip: issue, action, who handled it and the hour it opened and closed; hours to solve and a target check fill in by themselves.
One row per disruption: kind, the new plan, the extra cost, what the supplier refunded and what the client paid; the cost to the agency and a recovery check fill in by themselves.
One row per special request: kind, wording, the supplier asked and the answer; the confirmed flag, days waiting and a chase check fill in by themselves.
Post-trip tasks after a client returns
One row per follow-up task after a trip: welcome home, feedback, review, commission check, thank-you and referral; days late and a task check fill in by themselves.
The suppliers you book with: category, contact and phone; bookings made and bookings still ahead fill in by themselves.
Your clients with phone and kind; trips taken and documents still outstanding fill in by themselves.
The owner, four advisors and seven freelance specialists with phone and speciality; departures this month and in the next 7 days fill in by themselves.
Departures and documents complete by week
One row per week: trips leaving and how many had every document in on time; the ready rate, the weeks ahead and a target check fill in by themselves.
